messages.subject: Simulated two-dimensional Theta values
parts:
Hello, 

We can use the following code to simulate unidimensional theta values from a random normal distribution. What if we want to simulate two-dimensional theta values that are not totally independent (say with a correlation of .5)? Thanks a lot!

theta <- matrix(rnorm(100000))

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Simulated two-dimensional Theta values
parts:
You can always supply a matrix of theta's to simdata(), which means that you can generate the latent traits from any potential distribution and use those (e.g., compulas, skewed distribution, etc). 

Phil
